# UI and frontend quality — conditional

Activate this workflow only when the current task designs, builds, changes, or reviews a UI or frontend: layout, styling, components, interaction, accessibility, or browser-facing behavior. For backend-only, database, infrastructure, or unrelated documentation/script tasks, skip this workflow: do not load design skills, fetch the checklist, or run UI audits. In mixed tasks, apply it only to the UI/frontend portion.

1. Before UI work, read and follow the installed baseline-ui skill and other relevant design or stack skills. Add fixing-accessibility when the change touches interactive controls, forms, or dialogs, and fixing-motion-performance when it touches animation. Reuse the project's components, tokens, and design system; the project's existing stack takes precedence over a skill's stack defaults. If a required skill is unavailable, report that limitation instead of claiming it ran.
2. For a new UI with no Figma file or existing design system (a POC, prototype, or internal tool), pick one or two reference products from https://uiuxshowcase.com that match the product type before deciding layout, palette, and typography. Each showcase page links the live site and includes a full-page screenshot; use the screenshot when the live site serves text to automated browsers. Borrow structure and visual language (hierarchy, spacing, component treatment, color strategy), never logos, brand marks, or copy, and name the references you used in your response. A Figma file, an existing design system, or the project's own tokens always take precedence over the showcase.
3. For frontend work, consult https://github.com/thedaviddias/front-end-checklist and its linked rules for the changed surface. Use an existing Front-End Checklist skill or MCP integration if available; otherwise read the repository checklist directly. Check applicable accessibility, responsive layout, performance, HTML/CSS/JavaScript, images, SEO, security, privacy, internationalization, and testing guidance. Prioritize critical/high findings. Do not install packages or add MCP servers automatically, send private code to a public audit service, or expand a local fix into a site-wide audit. For native UI, use platform guidance and skip web-only rules.
4. Exercise the actual rendered surface and changed interactions. Check relevant viewport sizes, keyboard/focus behavior, labels/contrast, overflow, loading/error/empty states, and reduced motion when affected. Run the project's relevant checks; distinguish observed behavior from code inspection.
5. Before delivery, fix in-scope findings and briefly report verification evidence plus any blocked or unverified checks. If the checklist cannot be fetched, state that limitation and use the skill's local guidance without claiming full checklist compliance.

This is a conditional instruction, not an automatic audit or enforcement gate. Re-evaluate its scope when the task changes.
